note: Primary #92934. Windows: a synchronous PostToolUse command hook can delay the tool result until a persistent descendant exits, even though the configured hook process has already exited successfully. Separate from #90049.
title: Windows: synchronous PostToolUse delays tool results until a persistent child exits

stall.slowHook: Slow PostToolUse hooks: 91931ms for PowerShell (1 hooks)

expected: The tool result is delivered when hook.ps1 exits.
observed: The main tool completes, and hook.ps1 exits immediately, but Claude Code delays the tool result until child.ps1 exits about 90 seconds later.

separateFrom.why: does not require EnterWorktree; bounded wait rather than worktree-transition result-loss

asyncControl: Configuring the hook with async: true avoids the blocking path in this control.
mechanismNote: This is one controlled reproduction; it does not establish the internal mechanism.
